source_review.notes: Checked RFC 3986 query semantics, RFC 8288 linking, RFC 8977 as a scoped paging example, and maintained PostgreSQL 17 LIMIT/OFFSET documentation. Vendor execution notes are not generalized into universal datastore guarantees.

notation_and_syntax.notes: Membership, time, principal, predicate, tuple, direction, identity, and continuation notation is defined before use.

numerical_recomputation.notes: Illustrative counts and limits support scale examples but no numerical derivation is claimed.

evidence: mixed due ascending priority descending ID ascending predicate
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Forward lexicographic predicates were independently derived with direction reversal for descending components.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary review spans ordering, mutation, parsing, privacy, comparator evolution, and intermittent traversal.

invariant_checking.notes: Examples and answers preserve all five traversal invariants.

proof_review.notes: No formal datastore or traversal proof is claimed.

evidence: keyset is not called a snapshot
successful pages do not prove completeness
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No empirical benchmark or universal database claim is made, so artificial executable code was omitted.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed filter grammar, typed semantics, authorization, total ordering, offset/keyset/snapshot models, cursor design, counts, links, indexes, caches, and traversal tests.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed injection, parser differentials, protected filter/sort leakage, cursor integrity and scope, key rotation, collation upgrades, resource exhaustion, replica lag, and telemetry cardinality.

pedagogical_review.notes: Ten examples cover distinct traversal failures; five exercises progress from total-order definition through predicate derivation, cursor diagnosis, mechanism comparison, and disaster-response transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
